# Defects meet boundaries {#sec-defect-boundary}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false title="Learning goals"}
- Describe the doubled theory of a defect: why the reflected copy carries the opposite coproduct, so that the bulk symmetry is $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$, and why the reflected soliton is the conjugate multiplet.
- Recognize transparent defects and invertible lines as quantum symmetric pairs of diagonal type, twisted by the symmetry the line implements, and know what is proved about them and in which setting.
- Know which symmetry a jump defect keeps in the doubled picture: one Borel half untwisted and the other twisted by charge conjugation, on two different module structures of $\mathcal W$, with no coideal combining them.
- Fuse a defect onto a boundary, quantum mechanically and classically, and compare the result with the oscillator boundary of Baseilhac, Delius and George.
- Place defect–boundary fusion among the tensor K-matrices of Appel and Vlaar, and among the boundaries with non-invertible symmetries of Shimamori and Yamaguchi.
:::

The doubling trick of @sec-doubling-trick turns a defect into a boundary. Bajnok and George used it to derive the defect axioms from the boundary axioms [@bajnok_george2006], and @prp-doubling made this precise: the doubled reflection equation is the set of triangle relations, boundary unitarity is defect unitarity, and boundary crossing-unitarity is defect crossing. This chapter asks the question that @sec-boundary-qg asked for boundaries and @sec-defect-qg for defects: which symmetry does the doubled boundary preserve? @sec-qsp placed the boundary coideals of Part VII in the theory of quantum symmetric pairs. Here we do the same for the defects of @sec-defect-qg.

Three answers come out. A transparent defect, and more generally an invertible line, is a quantum symmetric pair of diagonal type, the case in which the quasi-K-matrix of Bao and Wang is Lusztig's quasi-R-matrix [@bao_wang2018b, Rem. 4.10(2)]. A jump defect is not. Its doubled boundary keeps the diagonal Borel subalgebra, with the defect space $\mathcal W$ as a dynamical boundary module, as was expected before the test; in addition it keeps the opposite Borel subalgebra twisted by charge conjugation, on a second module structure of $\mathcal W$. The two halves are those of the two invertible lines between which the defect interpolates as $\theta_d\to\pm\infty$ (@prp-defect-twist-limit). Finally, a defect in front of a boundary is a new boundary. For sine-Gordon solitons a type-I defect fused onto a Dirichlet boundary gives exactly the Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov reflection matrix, scalar factor included, with the defect rapidity as the second boundary parameter, and classically the fusion dresses the boundary K-matrix by the defect matrix $L_d$. The numerical checks are in `textbook_code/defect_doubling.py` (17 checks, about 30 s).

## The doubled theory {#sec-doubled-theory}

**The reflected copy.** In the doubled theory $\Phi(x)=(\vec\phi(x),\vec\psi(-x))$, $x\le0$, a $\vec\psi$-particle of rapidity $\theta$ becomes a particle of the second copy with rapidity $u=-\theta$, and the order of $\vec\psi$-particles is reversed (@sec-doubling-trick). As a representation, the reflected particle at rapidity $u$ is the original multiplet at rapidity $-u$; we write $V'(u)$ for it, so $V'(u)=V(-u)$ as a vector space with the action $\pi_{V(-u)}$. Its two-particle states appear in reversed order, and the symmetry, which acts on $\vec\psi$-particles through $\Delta$ in their original order, acts on the reflected order through $\Delta^{\rm op}$. Correspondingly, the reflected copy scatters with $P\check RP$ at the same rapidity difference (@sec-doubling-trick), and $P\check RP$ intertwines $\Delta^{\rm op}$ because $\check R$ intertwines $\Delta$. The algebra acting on the reflected copy is therefore $U^{\rm cop}$, the same algebra $U=U_q(\hat g)$ with the opposite coproduct.

Physically, $x\to-x$ exchanges left- and right-movers, and with them the non-local charges $Q_j$ and $\bar Q_j$ of @sec-nonlocal-charges, which become $e_j$ and $f_j$. The quantum Chevalley involution $\omega_q$ of (-@eq-omega-map) exchanges $e_j$ and $f_j$ and satisfies $\Delta\circ\omega_q=(\omega_q\otimes\omega_q)\circ\Delta^{\rm op}$, so it is a Hopf algebra isomorphism $U^{\rm cop}\to U$. Through it the reflected copy becomes an ordinary $U$-module, and it is the conjugate multiplet: in the principal gradation $V(1/y)\circ\omega_q=\bar V(y)$ exactly, with $\bar V$ as in @sec-an-diagonal-k. Parity maps solitons to antisolitons.

**The doubled symmetry.** The doubled theory has the bulk symmetry
$$
A=U\otimes U^{\rm cop},\qquad \Delta_A(g\otimes h)=\sum\big(g_{(1)}\otimes h_{(2)}\big)\otimes\big(g_{(2)}\otimes h_{(1)}\big),
$$ {#eq-dbd-coproduct}
in Sweedler's notation $\Delta(g)=\sum g_{(1)}\otimes g_{(2)}$. The first factor acts on the $\vec\phi$-copy and the second on the reflected copy: on $M(\theta)=V(\theta)\oplus V'(\theta)$, the element $g\otimes h$ acts as $\pi(g)\varepsilon(h)$ on $V$ and as $\varepsilon(g)\pi'(h)$ on $V'$, with $\varepsilon$ the counit. The doubled bulk S-matrix, $\check R$ on two $V$-particles, $P\check RP$ on two $V'$-particles and the flip on mixed pairs, commutes with $\Delta_A$: the flip does, because the two factors of $A$ act on different copies. The doubled K-matrix (-@eq-doubled-k) lives on $(V\oplus V')\otimes\mathcal W$ with $\mathcal W$ on the right, so $\mathcal W$ is a boundary module, and a symmetry of the doubled boundary is a left coideal subalgebra $B\subset A$, $\Delta_A(B)\subset A\otimes B$, acting on $\mathcal W$ through some representation $\chi$ and on $M(\theta)\otimes\mathcal W$ through $(\sigma\otimes\chi)\Delta_A$, exactly as for the coideals of @sec-coideal.

::: {#prp-reflected-copy}
## The reflected copy
**[Established; numerically checked]** (1) The reflected copy carries the $U^{\rm cop}$-modules $V'(u)=V(-u)$, and its S-matrix $P\check R(x_1/x_2)P$ intertwines $\Delta^{\rm op}$. (2) The doubled bulk S-matrix intertwines $\Delta_A$ of $A=U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$, and not the coproduct of $U\otimes U$. (3) Through $\omega_q$, $V'(u)$ is the conjugate multiplet $\bar V(u)$, and $P\check R(1/y_2,1/y_1)P=\check R_{\bar V\bar V}(y_1/y_2)$ up to a scalar. (4) The doubled K-matrix (-@eq-doubled-k) is a K-matrix of the doubled theory with boundary module $\mathcal W$; its reflection equation is equivalent to the triangle relations (@prp-doubling).
:::

::: {.proof}
(1) $P\Delta(a)P=\Delta^{\rm op}(a)$. (2) On pairs within one copy this is (1) and its analogue for $\check R$; on mixed pairs the action of $A$ factorizes as $\pi(g)\otimes\pi'(h)$, which the flip intertwines. With $\Delta$ in place of $\Delta^{\rm op}$ on the second factor, the $V'V'$ block would need $P\check RP$ to intertwine $\Delta$. (3) $\omega_q$ is a Hopf isomorphism $U^{\rm cop}\to U$, and $V(1/y)\circ\omega_q$ has $e_j\mapsto yF_j$, $f_j\mapsto E_j/y$, $k_j\mapsto k_j^{-1}$, which is $\bar V(y)$; uniqueness of the intertwiner gives the statement about $\check R$. (4) is @prp-doubling.
:::

We checked (2) and (3) for the sine-Gordon solitons and the $a_2^{(1)}$ vector solitons: the doubled $\check R$ commutes with $\Delta_A$ to $10^{-15}$ and fails by 1.7 with $U\otimes U$; for sine-Gordon $\bar V(y)=CV(y)C$ with $C=\sigma_x$ (`textbook_code/defect_doubling.py`). The equivalence (4) is checked in `textbook_code/defect_axioms.py`.

## Transparent defects and diagonal symmetric pairs {#sec-diagonal-qsp}

**The diagonal coideal.** The transparent defect has $\mathcal W=\mathbb C$ and $\mathbb T=\bar{\mathbb T}=1$; its doubled K-matrix exchanges the copies. Its symmetry is the image of the bulk symmetry,
$$
\Delta(U)=\Big\{\sum a_{(1)}\otimes a_{(2)}\ :\ a\in U\Big\}\subset U\otimes U^{\rm cop},\qquad
\Delta_A\big(\Delta(a)\big)=\sum\big(a_{(1)}\otimes a_{(3)}\big)\otimes\Delta\big(a_{(2)}\big),
$$ {#eq-dbd-diagonal}
which is a left coideal subalgebra by coassociativity, with $\mathcal W=\mathbb C$ carrying the counit. More generally, for any Hopf algebra automorphism $\psi$ of $U$, such as a torus rescaling $e_j\to t_je_j$, $f_j\to f_j/t_j$ or a diagram automorphism, $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$ is a left coideal subalgebra, a **twisted diagonal**. An invertible line implements a symmetry of the bulk: $\mathcal W=\mathbb C$ and $\mathbb T$ an invertible matrix on $V$ with $\mathbb T\pi(a)\mathbb T^{-1}=\pi(\psi(a))$ for some $\psi$. Its doubled boundary is invariant under $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$. The twist defect $\mathbb T=e^{i\alpha\cdot\mu}$ of @prp-twist-defect gives a torus twist, $t_1=1/t_0=e^{2i\alpha}$ for sine-Gordon, and the charge-conjugation line $\mathbb T=C$ gives the diagram automorphism $\tau$ that exchanges the nodes $0$ and $1$. A particle frozen as a defect, $\mathcal W=V(\theta_d)$ and $\mathbb T=\check R$ (@sec-triangle-relations), is invariant under the untwisted $\Delta(U)$, with $U$ acting on $\mathcal W$ by its representation.

**Quantum symmetric pairs of diagonal type.** Bao and Wang call $(U\otimes U,U)$, with $U$ embedded by $\varphi=(\omega\otimes1)\circ\Delta$, the quantum symmetric pair of diagonal type [@bao_wang2018b, Rem. 4.10(2)]. Their $\omega$ is our $\omega_q$ and their coproduct is that of Part VI, and their coideals are right coideals, as Kolb's are (@sec-letzter-kolb). The map $\omega_q\otimes{\rm id}:U\otimes U^{\rm cop}\to U\otimes U$ is an algebra isomorphism and a coalgebra anti-isomorphism, since each factor reverses the coproduct, so it maps left coideals to right coideals, and it maps $\Delta(U)$ of (-@eq-dbd-diagonal) onto $\varphi(U)$. This is the analogue of @prp-omega-dictionary. At $q=1$, $\varphi(\mathfrak g)$ is the fixed-point algebra of the involution $(x,y)\mapsto(\omega(y),\omega(x))$ of $\mathfrak g\oplus\mathfrak g$, of the second kind like all the involutions of @sec-symmetric-pairs. Its Satake diagram is two copies of the Dynkin diagram, all nodes white, with $\tau$ exchanging corresponding nodes (by hand). The physical reading is the one above: a boundary of the doubled theory pairs each charge of the $\vec\phi$-copy with the charge of the opposite chirality of the reflected copy.

::: {#prp-diagonal-coideal}
## Transparent defects and invertible lines are diagonal-type pairs
**[Theorem (1)–(2); Established (3); Numerical (4)]** (1) For every Hopf automorphism $\psi$ of $U$, $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$ is a left coideal subalgebra of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$. (2) The doubled boundary of an invertible line with $\mathbb T\pi(\cdot)\mathbb T^{-1}=\pi\circ\psi$, and in particular of the transparent defect ($\psi={\rm id}$), is invariant under it. (3) $(\omega_q\otimes{\rm id})\Delta(U)$ is the coideal of the quantum symmetric pair of diagonal type, whose quasi-K-matrix is Lusztig's quasi-R-matrix twisted by $\omega\otimes1$ [@bao_wang2018b, Rem. 4.10(2)] [@wang2023, Ex. 0.1 and Sec. 2]. (4) Let $X$ be the space spanned by the 21 monomials $g\otimes h$ of degree at most one in the generators of one node of each factor ($g,h\in\{k^{-1},1,k,e,f\}$). For the transparent defect (sine-Gordon solitons, a spin-1 probe, the $a_2$ vector solitons), the twist line and the charge-conjugation line, the largest left coideal contained in the commutant of the doubled K-matrix in $X$ is exactly $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)\cap X$, spanned by $1$, $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(k^{\pm1})$, $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(e)$ and $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(f)$.
:::

::: {.proof}
(1) $\Delta_A\big((1\otimes\psi)\Delta(a)\big)=\sum\big(a_{(1)}\otimes\psi(a_{(3)})\big)\otimes(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(a_{(2)})$, by (-@eq-dbd-diagonal) and because $\psi$ is a coalgebra map. (2) On a one-particle state $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(a)$ acts as $\pi(a)$ on $V$ and as $\pi(\psi(a))$ on $V'$, and the off-diagonal blocks of $K$ are $\mathbb T$ and $\bar{\mathbb T}=\mathbb T^{-1}$; the coideal property carries this to many-particle states, as in @thm-k-reflection. (3) is quoted. (4) is numerical (`textbook_code/defect_doubling.py`).
:::

The search in (4) shows why the coideal property matters. In $X$ the commutant of the doubled K-matrix on one-particle states is 17-dimensional: it contains, for example, $e\otimes1+1\otimes e$, which acts identically on the two copies of a single particle but fails on a $V\otimes V'$ pair. Imposing the two-particle doubled reflection leaves 7 or 12 dimensions, depending on the probe, because symmetric combinations of Cartan elements of the two copies cannot be distinguished with two particles. Requiring $\Delta_A(S)\subset A\otimes S$, iterated to a fixed point, removes all of this and leaves the 5-dimensional twisted diagonal, to $10^{-15}$, in every case. The procedure is the numerical counterpart of a theorem of Appel and Vlaar: a quantum symmetric pair subalgebra is the largest coideal subalgebra contained in the fixed points of a certain automorphism built from the universal K-matrix [@appel_vlaar2024, Thm. 4.1.3].

**What is proved, and where.** Bao and Wang's remark is stated in the finite-type setting of their paper, with "one checks" for the coideal property [@bao_wang2018b, Sec. 1.2 and Rem. 4.10]. Wang's survey repeats it as an example and states that the quasi-K-matrix of the diagonal type reduces to the quasi-R-matrix [@wang2023, Ex. 0.1 and Sec. 2]. Balagović and Kolb construct the quasi-K-matrix in general and do not discuss the diagonal type [@balagovic_kolb2019]. For affine $\hat g$ the relevant Cartan matrix, that of $\hat g\oplus\hat g$, is decomposable, and Kolb [@kolb2014] and Appel and Vlaar [@appel_vlaar2022] assume an indecomposable one, so their theorems do not cover the diagonal type of affine algebras as stated. Nothing is lost for the physics: for the diagonal type the role of the universal K-matrix is played by the universal R-matrix, which exists for $U_q(\hat g)$ (@sec-universal-r-affine), and the doubled K-matrix of a particle used as a defect is its evaluation. Kolb and Yakimov's "symmetric pairs for Nichols algebras of diagonal type" [@kolb_yakimov2020] concern Nichols algebras with diagonal braiding, an unrelated use of the word.

In conformal field theory the folded image of the trivial defect is the boundary state of the doubled theory that glues the two copies by the identity, which preserves the diagonal chiral algebra; (-@eq-dbd-diagonal) is its massive, quantum-group counterpart.

## Jump defects in the doubled picture {#sec-jump-coideal}

For a jump defect $\mathcal W$ is infinite dimensional and $\mathbb T$ depends on $\theta-\theta_d$. The following conjecture, and the expectation stated after it, were registered when this part was planned, before the test was run.

::: {#cnj-twisted-diagonal}
## Twisted diagonal symmetry of a jump defect
**[Conjecture; refuted as stated by the test in `textbook_code/defect_doubling.py`]** The doubled boundary (-@eq-doubled-k) of a type-I defect is invariant under a twisted diagonal coideal $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$ of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$, with $\mathcal W$ a module of it.
:::

The expectation stated with it was that the conjecture is false as stated: a type-I$_-$ defect keeps only the Borel subalgebra $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$ (@sec-borel), so the full diagonal cannot survive, and the likely truth is that a diagonal Borel subalgebra acts, with $\mathcal W$ a dynamical boundary module. The test confirms this and adds a second, twisted, Borel symmetry.

**The test.** A generator $x$ of $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$ acts on $M(\theta)\otimes\mathcal W$ through (-@eq-dbd-coproduct). For $x=e_j\otimes1+k_j\otimes\psi(e_j)$ this action is $\pi(e_j)\otimes1+\pi(k_j)\otimes Y$ on $V\otimes\mathcal W$ and $1\otimes Y+\pi'(\psi(e_j))\otimes\kappa$ on $V'\otimes\mathcal W$, with unknown operators $Y=\chi(x)$ and $\kappa=\chi(k_j\otimes\psi(k_j))$ on $\mathcal W$; the generators $f_j$ are analogous. The equation $K(\theta)X(\theta)=X(-\theta)K(\theta)$ is linear and inhomogeneous in the unknowns. We solved it by least squares for three rapidities at once, with $\theta$-independent unknowns of the right weight, on windows $\lvert n\rvert\le N$ with $N=5,7,9$ and equations imposed on $\lvert n\rvert\le N-2$. A torus factor in $\psi$ is absorbed into $\kappa$, so the cases $\psi(e_j)\propto e_j$ ("id") and $\psi(e_j)\propto e_{\tau(j)}$ ("$\tau$") cover all twisted diagonals of $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ built from these automorphisms.

::: {#prp-diagonal-borel}
## The two Borel symmetries of a jump defect
**[Theorem (1), (4); Numerical (2), (3), (5)]** Let $\mathbb T$ be the sine-Gordon transmission matrix of type I$_\mp$ on the Weyl module $\mathcal W$ of $U_q(\mathfrak b^\mp)$, (-@eq-sg-transmission-matrix) and @prp-two-borels.

1. The diagonal Borel subalgebra $\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^\mp))$ is a left coideal subalgebra of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$, and the doubled boundary is invariant under it, with $\mathcal W$ the Weyl module.
2. The opposite Borel subalgebra twisted by charge conjugation, $(1\otimes\tau)\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^\pm))$, is also a symmetry, with a second module structure $\tilde\rho$ on $\mathcal W$. For type I$_-$, in the normalization of (-@eq-sg-transmission-matrix), with $a=iy_dq^{-s}/(q^2-1)$ and $b=iy_dq^{s}/(q^2-1)$,

   $$
   \tilde\rho(e_1)\lvert n\rangle=a\,q^{-2n}\lvert n+1\rangle,\quad \tilde\rho(k_1)\lvert n\rangle=q^{-2n-2-s}\lvert n+2\rangle,\quad
   \tilde\rho(e_0)\lvert n\rangle=b\,q^{2n}\lvert n-1\rangle,\quad \tilde\rho(k_0)\lvert n\rangle=q^{2n-2+s}\lvert n-2\rangle .
   $$ {#eq-dbd-second-module}

3. No twisted diagonal $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$ is a symmetry: for type I$_-$ the untwisted $e_j$ and the $\tau$-twisted $f_j$ fail, for type I$_+$ the untwisted $f_j$ and the $\tau$-twisted $e_j$.
4. No coideal subalgebra of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$ containing both Borel symmetries acts on any module $\mathcal W$ compatibly with the doubled K-matrix.
5. As $\theta_d\to+\infty$ the untwisted diagonal is restored, as $\theta_d\to-\infty$ the $\tau$-twisted one.
:::

::: {.proof}
(1) $U_q(\mathfrak b^\mp)$ is a Hopf subalgebra, so (-@eq-dbd-diagonal) holds within it. On $V\otimes\mathcal W$ the action of $\Delta(b)$ is $(\pi\otimes\rho)\Delta(b)$ and on $V'\otimes\mathcal W$ it is $(\pi'\otimes\rho)\Delta^{\rm op}(b)$, so the block $P\mathbb T$ of $K$ intertwines them exactly when $\mathbb T$ satisfies (-@eq-borel-intertwiner); the block $\bar{\mathbb T}P$ follows by unitarity. (2) For $x=e_1\otimes1+k_1\otimes e_0$ the matrix elements of the intertwining equation on $v_\pm\otimes\lvert n\rangle$ give, with $\mathbb T$ in the notation of @prp-sg-t-unique, $Y_{n+1}-Y_n=-iy_dq^{-2n-2-s}$ and $\kappa_n=q^{-2n-2-s}$, with no dependence on $\theta$; $\tilde\rho(k_1)Y\tilde\rho(k_1)^{-1}=q^2Y$ fixes the free constant in $Y$, and $e_0$ is analogous (@exr-dbd-mixed-twist). Then $\tilde\rho(k_0)\tilde\rho(k_1)=1$, $\tilde\rho(k_i)\tilde\rho(e_j)\tilde\rho(k_i)^{-1}=q^{a_{ij}}\tilde\rho(e_j)$, and $\tilde\rho(e_1)\tilde\rho(e_0)=\tilde\rho(e_0)\tilde\rho(e_1)=abq^2$ is central, so the $q$-Serre relations hold as for the Weyl module. (4) In $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$, $\Delta(k_1)\big(e_1\otimes1+k_1\otimes e_0\big)\Delta(k_1)^{-1}=q^2e_1\otimes1+q^{-2}k_1\otimes e_0$, so any subalgebra containing both contains $e_1\otimes1$ when $q^4\ne1$. Its action on $V\otimes\mathcal W$ is $\pi(e_1)\otimes1+\pi(k_1)\otimes Z$ and on $V'\otimes\mathcal W$ it is $1\otimes Z$; the matrix element of $\mathbb T(\pi(e_1)\otimes1)$ proportional to $C_n$ grows like $y^2$ and has nothing to cancel against (@exr-dbd-e-one). (3), (5) are numerical.
:::

The numbers: in (1) the residual is $2\times10^{-15}$ for both types, windows $N=6,8$ and offsets $s=0,0.3$; in (2) and the corresponding tests for type I$_+$, at most $6\times10^{-15}$ on all windows. The failing generators in (3) leave minimal residuals between 0.93 and 0.97, stable from $N=5$ to $N=9$; the operator $\tilde\rho(k_1)$ commutes with $\rho(k_1)={\rm diag}(q^{2n+s})$ only up to $q^4$, although $k_1\otimes k_1$ and $k_1\otimes k_0$ commute in $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$, and $e_1\otimes1$ fails with residual 0.96. In (5), for $N=6$ the untwisted $e$-generator leaves the residuals 0.44, 0.063, 0.008 at $\theta_d=1.5$, 3, 4.5, falling roughly like $e^{-\lambda\theta_d}$, and the $\tau$-twisted $f$-generator leaves 0.27, 0.036, 0.005 at $\theta_d=-1.5,-3,-4.5$ (`textbook_code/defect_doubling.py`).

**Reading the result.** As $\theta-\theta_d\to-\infty$ the type-I$_-$ defect becomes a superposition of twist lines, one for each value of the defect charge, and as $\theta-\theta_d\to+\infty$ the charge-conjugation line dressed by a shift of the defect charge (@prp-defect-twist-limit). Each of these invertible lines has a full twisted diagonal symmetry. At finite $\theta_d$ the defect keeps one Borel half of each: the half $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$ of the twist line's diagonal, and the half $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ of the charge-conjugation line's diagonal. This is the quantum form of the massless defect (-@eq-dq-massless-defect), which passes one chirality and charge-conjugates the other. The second module structure has an equally concrete origin. The map $\psi\to-\psi$ takes type I$_-$ to type I$_+$ (@prp-two-borels (3)), and on the doubled theory it acts as charge conjugation on the reflected copy, that is, as $\tau$ on the second factor of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$. The $\tau$-twisted $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ is therefore the $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ symmetry of the same defect read as a type-I$_+$ defect, whose charge is the other combination $-(a+b)$ of Bowcock, Corrigan and Zambon's two labels; in the one-label module that combination is not diagonal, and its $q$-power acts as the shift $\tilde\rho(k_1)$. (This is an interpretation; the check is (2).) Part (4) shows that the two Borel halves are genuinely separate: they are symmetries of the same operator, but not the image of one coideal acting on one module. In particular @prp-diagonal-borel corrects nothing in @sec-borel, where it was shown that the $e_j$ do not extend the symmetry with the untwisted coproduct; they survive twisted.

**Beyond sine-Gordon.** For $a_r^{(1)}$ the limits of the type-I$_-$ defect are again twist lines as $\theta_d\to+\infty$, but as $\theta_d\to-\infty$ the defect becomes the invertible line of the rotation $\pi$ of the affine Dynkin diagram (@prp-an-defect-delay), the same $\pi$ that enters $\mathsf D=2(1-\pi)^{-1}$ (-@eq-d-matrix). For $a_1^{(1)}$ the rotation is the node exchange $\tau$. The natural expectation is therefore that the doubled boundary of an $a_r^{(1)}$ type-I$_-$ defect keeps $\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^-))$ and the rotation-twisted $(1\otimes\pi)\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^+))$, the latter on a second module structure of $\mathcal W$. @prp-dpt-doubled confirms this for type I$_-$ of $a_2^{(1)}$ and $a_3^{(1)}$, with the transmission matrices of @sec-soliton-transmission and $\pi(e_j)=e_{j-1}$; the opposite rotation fails. The module relations of the second structure have not been checked.

**The RTT algebra inside the doubled reflection-equation algebra.** Write the off-diagonal blocks of (-@eq-doubled-k) in fixed slots, $P\mathbb T(\theta)=\mathbb L(\theta)$ and $\bar{\mathbb T}(\theta)P=\mathbb L(-\theta)^{-1}$ by (-@eq-defect-unitarity). The doubled reflection equation splits into blocks according to the copies of the two incoming particles (@prp-doubling): the block from $VV$ to $V'V'$ is the RTT relation (-@eq-triangle-rtt) for $\mathbb L$, the block from $V'V'$ to $VV$ is the same relation for $\mathbb L^{-1}$, and the mixed blocks are the relations between $\mathbb L$ and $\mathbb L^{-1}$ that follow from it. So the reflection-equation algebra of the doubled theory, restricted to off-diagonal K-matrices, is the Yang–Baxter algebra of @tbl-boundary-defect-algebra with its inverse adjoined: the bialgebra of the defect sits inside the comodule algebra of the doubled boundary. The coideals behave in the same way. A Borel subalgebra is a Hopf subalgebra of $U$, and its diagonal image is a coideal of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$ that is again a Hopf algebra, isomorphic to $U_q(\mathfrak b^\mp)$, which is why the doubled boundary can carry a module of the same kind as the defect itself.

**$\mathcal W$ as a dynamical boundary module.** In the sense of @sec-dynamical-boundary, the doubled boundary of a jump defect is a dynamical boundary: the boundary algebra $\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^\mp))\cong U_q(\mathfrak b^\mp)$ acts on the boundary space $\mathcal W$, a $q$-oscillator Weyl module (-@eq-weyl-module), and the K-matrix is its intertwiner. Baseilhac and Koizumi's quantized oscillator boundary of sine-Gordon theory is also a dynamical boundary with an infinite-dimensional boundary module, but of the $q$-Onsager algebra of @sec-q-onsager [@baseilhac_koizumi2003]. The two kinds of boundary are compared classically in @sec-defect-boundary-fusion.

| Line | Defect space $\mathcal W$ | Symmetry of the doubled boundary | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| transparent, $\mathbb T=1$ | $\mathbb C$ | $\Delta(U)$; diagonal type [@bao_wang2018b] | [Theorem]; maximal coideal [Numerical] |
| twist line $e^{i\alpha\cdot\mu}$ | $\mathbb C$ | $(1\otimes t)\Delta(U)$, $t$ a torus twist | [Theorem]; [Numerical] |
| charge conjugation $C$ | $\mathbb C$ | $(1\otimes\tau)\Delta(U)$ | [Theorem]; [Numerical] |
| particle as defect, $\mathbb T=\check R$ | $V(\theta_d)$ | $\Delta(U)$, $U$ acting on $\mathcal W$ | [Theorem]; [Numerical] |
| type I$_-$ jump | Weyl module of $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$ | $\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^-))$ on $\rho$ and $(1\otimes\tau)\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^+))$ on $\tilde\rho$; no twisted diagonal | [Numerical]; $\tilde\rho$ and (4) by hand |
| type I$_+$ jump | Weyl module of $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ | $\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^+))$ and $(1\otimes\tau)\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^-))$ | [Numerical] |
| type I$_-$, $\theta_d\to+\infty$ / $-\infty$ | as above | $(1\otimes t_n)\Delta(U)$ / $(1\otimes\tau)\Delta(U)$ restored | [Numerical] |

: Symmetries of the doubled boundaries of sine-Gordon lines. $\tau$ exchanges the nodes $0,1$; $t_n$ depends on the defect charge. {#tbl-dbd-symmetries}

## Fusing defects onto boundaries {#sec-defect-boundary-fusion}

**The fused reflection matrix.** Let a defect stand in front of a boundary with reflection matrix $K(\theta):V(\theta)\to V(-\theta)$. A particle crosses the defect, is reflected, and crosses back, so the composite is a boundary with boundary module $\mathcal W$ and reflection matrix
$$
K_{\rm f}(\theta)=\bar{\mathbb T}(\theta)\,\big(1_{\mathcal W}\otimes K(\theta)\big)\,\mathbb T(\theta):\ V(\theta)\otimes\mathcal W\to V(-\theta)\otimes\mathcal W ,
$$ {#eq-dbd-fused-k}
with $\mathcal W$ on the right as in @sec-doubling-trick, and $\bar{\mathbb T}(\theta)=\mathbb T(-\theta)^{-1}$. This is Sklyanin's dressing of a K-matrix [@sklyanin1988], Bajnok and George's (19) [@bajnok_george2006] and Corrigan and Zambon's (2.9) [@cz2012], whose $\hat T(\theta)=T(-\theta)^{-1}$ is our $\bar{\mathbb T}$. For scalar factors it is the fusion $K'=\bar{\mathbb T}K\mathbb T$ of @sec-doubling-trick, and for the scaling Lee–Yang model it gives $K_b=\bar{\mathbb T}_bK_{(\mathbb 1)}\mathbb T_b$ (@sec-defect-lee-yang).

::: {#prp-defect-fusion-k}
## Defect–boundary fusion
**[Theorem (1); Numerical (2)–(3); by hand (4)]** (1) If $K$ satisfies the reflection equation and boundary unitarity, and $\mathbb T$ the triangle relations and defect unitarity, then (-@eq-dbd-fused-k) satisfies the reflection equation (-@eq-reflection-braid) on $V\otimes V\otimes\mathcal W$ and boundary unitarity. (2) **Sinh-Gordon** [@bajnok_simon2008]: $\bar{\mathbb T}_{\rm shG}(\theta)K_D(\theta;E)\mathbb T_{\rm shG}(\theta)=K_{\rm shG}(\theta;E,F=2i\theta_d/\pi)$, with $K_{\rm shG}$ of (-@eq-shg-reflection). (3) **Sine-Gordon solitons.** Let $\mathbb T$ be the type-I$_-$ matrix (-@eq-sg-transmission-matrix) with its scalar factor (-@eq-sgd-scalar), and $K_D$ the Dirichlet reflection matrix, the limit $\vartheta\to\infty$ of (-@eq-bsg-k-full) at $\eta=\eta_D$. Then $K_{\rm f}$ conserves the total topological charge, and on each charge sector $\{v_+\otimes\lvert n\rangle,v_-\otimes\lvert n+1\rangle\}$ it is, after a diagonal change of basis, the Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov matrix (-@eq-bsg-k-full) with
$$
\eta=\eta_D,\qquad\vartheta=\lambda\,\theta_d ,
$$
scalar factor included. (4) Combined with the classical fusion of @sec-sg-breather-transmission and the classical limit of @cnj-bsg-uv-ir, (3) is consistent exactly when $\lambda\theta_d=(\lambda+1)\theta_d^{\rm cl}$, which is the sine-Gordon form of @cnj-defect-parameter.
:::

::: {.proof}
(1) Each side of the reflection equation for $K_{\rm f}$ can be reduced, by the triangle relations, to $\bar{\mathbb T}\bar{\mathbb T}$ times a side of the reflection equation for $K$ times $\mathbb T\mathbb T$, as in Sklyanin's dressing; unitarity follows from $\bar{\mathbb T}(-\theta)\mathbb T(\theta)=1$. (2) $\bar{\mathbb T}_{\rm shG}\mathbb T_{\rm shG}=(\cosh\theta_d+i\sinh\theta)/(\cosh\theta_d-i\sinh\theta)$, which is $1/\big((1-F)(1+F)\big)$ at $\cos\frac{\pi F}2=\cosh\theta_d$ (@exr-sgd-fusion). (3) The block structure follows from the charge conservation of $\mathbb T$ and $K_D$; the identification is numerical. (4) Classically the fused boundary has $C_{0,1}=\cosh(\theta_d^{\rm cl}\pm\frac{i\beta_{\rm SG}\phi_D}2)$, so the classical limit of @cnj-bsg-uv-ir gives $\eta/(\lambda+1)=\beta_{\rm SG}\phi_D/2$, which is (-@eq-bsg-dirichlet), and $\vartheta/(\lambda+1)=\theta_d^{\rm cl}$ (@exr-dbd-fusion-gz).
:::

We checked (3) on windows $N=5,7,9$: the gauge invariants $K_{++}/K_{--}$ and $K_{+-}K_{-+}/(K_{++}K_{--})$ of the sector blocks do not depend on $n$ ($2\times10^{-15}$) and agree with (-@eq-bsg-k-matrix) at $(\eta_D,\lambda\theta_d)$ ($10^{-15}$), while $\vartheta=-\lambda\theta_d$ or $\vartheta=\theta_d$ fail; $K_{\rm f}$ solves the reflection equation on the windows ($10^{-15}$) and a label-dependent perturbation of it does not. With the scalar factors, $\sigma(i\vartheta,u)\to1$ as $\vartheta\to\infty$, so $K_D=R_0(u)\sigma(\eta_D,u)/(2\cos\eta_D)\,{\rm diag}(ye^{i\eta_D}+y^{-1}e^{-i\eta_D},ye^{-i\eta_D}+y^{-1}e^{i\eta_D})$, and the diagonal entries of $K_{\rm f}$ agree with those of (-@eq-bsg-k-full) to $3\times10^{-9}$, the accuracy of our summation of the scalar factor at complex rapidity. Item (2) is re-checked to $10^{-16}$ (`textbook_code/defect_doubling.py`).

The matrix part of (3) is Corrigan and Zambon's observation that a type-I defect fused onto a Dirichlet boundary gives the Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov solution, with a dependence on the boundary charge that a similarity transformation removes [@cz2012, eqs. (2.16)–(2.18)]. The new points are the parameter map, the scalar factor (so no CDD factor appears), and (4): the soliton sector gives the same renormalization of the defect rapidity as the sinh-Gordon breathers in @sec-sg-breather-transmission. The infinite dimension of $\mathcal W$ is visible only in the bookkeeping of the topological charge: a type-I defect fused onto a Dirichlet boundary is an ordinary boundary. Corrigan and Zambon found that a type-II defect, by contrast, produces reflection matrices whose dependence on the boundary charge cannot be removed [@cz2012, eq. (2.19)], and Bajnok and Simon that a defect fused onto a Neumann boundary multiplies its reflection factor by a boundary CDD factor [@bajnok_simon2008, eqs. (19)–(20)].

**The classical version.** Let the defect at $x=0$ be followed by a boundary for $\vec\psi$ with a field-independent K-matrix $K_\psi(\lambda)$ satisfying (-@eq-boundary-compatibility), and let the region between them shrink to zero (@sec-sg-breather-transmission). The defect matrix relates the auxiliary solutions on the two sides, $\Psi_\phi=L_d\Psi_\psi$ (@sec-defect-lax), so the transport into the $\vec\psi$ region is $L_d(\lambda)^{-1}$ and the double-row transfer matrix (-@eq-double-row) of the composite system has the boundary matrix
$$
K_\phi(\lambda)=\sigma\big(L_d(1/\lambda)^{-1}\big)\,K_\psi(\lambda)\,L_d(\lambda)^{-1},
$$ {#eq-dbd-dressed-k}
which depends on the boundary values $\vec\phi(0)$, $\vec\psi(0)$: a dynamical K-matrix. It is the classical form of (-@eq-dbd-fused-k), with the inverse defect matrices that @prp-defect-transfer found for the defect operator.

::: {#prp-fused-bdg}
## Fused boundaries and the oscillator boundary
**[Theorem, by hand; numerically checked]** (1) On the fused system, (-@eq-dbd-dressed-k) satisfies $\partial_tK_\phi=K_\phi\,a_t(\lambda)+\sigma\big(a_t(1/\lambda)\big)K_\phi$, so ${\rm tr}\big(K_\phi(\lambda)\mathcal T(\lambda)\big)$ is conserved. This holds for every $a_r^{(1)}$ boundary of @tbl-durham, including Neumann, and both defect types (checked for type I$_-$). (2) The sine-Gordon defect potential (-@eq-sg-defect-potential) of type I$_-$ is the oscillator Hamiltonian (-@eq-bsg-oscillator) at the complex values
$$
\hat p=\frac{\beta_{\rm SG}\psi}2-i\theta_d,\qquad\hat q=\frac{\beta_{\rm SG}\psi}2+i\theta_d ,
$$
up to a constant. A defect fused onto the Dirichlet boundary $\psi=\phi_D$ is the static Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov boundary with $C_1=\cos\hat q=\cosh(\theta_d-\frac{i\beta_{\rm SG}\phi_D}2)$ and $C_0=\cos\hat p$: the oscillator frozen at a complex point. (3) A defect fused onto a Neumann boundary is a dynamical boundary with one boundary variable $\psi(t)$, conjugate to $\phi(0)$ through the defect's kinetic term (-@eq-dc-defect-bracket). It is not the boundary of Baseilhac, Delius and George: there $(\hat p,\hat q)$ is an independent canonical pair, the boundary condition has no $\partial_t\psi$ term, and the oscillator flow does not preserve $\hat p-\hat q=-2i\theta_d$.
:::

::: {.proof}
(1) From $\partial_tL_d=L_d\,a_t(\psi)-a_t(\phi)\,L_d$ (@sec-defect-lax), $\partial_t(L_d^{-1})=L_d^{-1}a_t(\phi)-a_t(\psi)L_d^{-1}$ and the same with $\sigma$ applied at $1/\lambda$. Hence $\partial_tK_\phi-K_\phi a_t(\phi;\lambda)-\sigma(a_t(\phi;1/\lambda))K_\phi=\sigma(L_d(1/\lambda)^{-1})\big[-K_\psi a_t(\psi;\lambda)-\sigma(a_t(\psi;1/\lambda))K_\psi\big]L_d(\lambda)^{-1}$, which vanishes by (-@eq-boundary-compatibility) for $\vec\psi$, since in the limit $\partial_x\vec\psi(0)$ obeys both the defect condition and the boundary condition. (2) Expand the cosines: $\sigma\cos\frac{\beta(\phi+\psi)}2+\sigma^{-1}\cos\frac{\beta(\phi-\psi)}2=e^{i\beta\phi/2}\cos(\frac{\beta\psi}2+i\theta_d)+e^{-i\beta\phi/2}\cos(\frac{\beta\psi}2-i\theta_d)$ with $\sigma=e^{-\theta_d}$ and $\beta=\beta_{\rm SG}$. (3) With Neumann conditions the defect conditions (-@eq-sg-defect-conditions) become $\partial_x\phi=\partial_t\psi-\partial_\phi\mathcal B_d$ and $\partial_t\phi=-\partial_\psi\mathcal B_d$ at $x=0$ [@bajnok_simon2008, eq. (5)], while the oscillator boundary has $\partial_x\phi=-\partial_\phi H_{\rm osc}$ and $\frac{d}{dt}(\hat p-\hat q)=-\frac{m_0}2\big(e^{i\beta\phi/2}\sin\hat q+e^{-i\beta\phi/2}\sin\hat p\big)\ne0$ on the line.
:::

Item (1) was checked with finite differences, at random field values on the fused system, for $a_1^{(1)}$ with a Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov boundary and with Neumann, $a_2^{(1)}$ with $C=(1,-1,1)$ and with Neumann, and $a_3^{(1)}$ with $C=(1,-1,1,-1)$ ($10^{-9}$); with $L_d$ in place of $L_d^{-1}$, or with $K_\psi$ undressed, it fails at order one. Items (2) and (3) were checked with sympy (`textbook_code/defect_doubling.py`). Item (1) gives, for $a_n^{(1)}$ with $n\ge2$, dynamical boundaries with $n$ boundary variables and a conserved generating function: a type-I defect fused onto a boundary of @tbl-durham. Part VII's problem 9 (@sec-boundary-open-problems) asked for such boundaries; whether the conserved quantities are in involution, and what the quantum versions are, we have not examined.

The oscillator boundary and the fused boundary are thus related but not equal. Both have the same boundary potential, but in the fused system one combination of the oscillator variables is frozen at $-2i\theta_d$ and the other is tied to the bulk field by the defect's symplectic structure. In the quantum theory the difference is equally clear: fused onto Dirichlet, the $q$-oscillator space $\mathcal W$ of the defect decouples (@prp-defect-fusion-k (3)), while in Baseilhac and Koizumi's quantized oscillator boundary the boundary module is an infinite-dimensional representation of the $q$-Onsager algebra [@baseilhac_koizumi2003].

## Tensor K-matrices {#sec-tensor-k}

Appel and Vlaar turned the fusion formula into a universal statement [@appel_vlaar2024]. For a quantum symmetric pair $U_q(\mathfrak k)\subset U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of Kac–Moody type, with their universal K-matrix $\mathcal K$ and twist automorphism $\psi$ (@sec-universal-k), they define the **tensor K-matrix**
$$
\mathbb K=\mathcal R^\psi_{21}\,(1\otimes\mathcal K)\,\mathcal R ,
$$
and prove that it lies in a completion of $U_q(\mathfrak k)\otimes U_q(\mathfrak g)$, satisfies a twisted intertwining identity, coproduct identities, and a generalized reflection equation on triple tensor products [@appel_vlaar2024, Thm. 5.6.1, eqs. (5.5)–(5.8)]. So $\mathbb K$ acts on $M\otimes V$ with $M$ only a $U_q(\mathfrak k)$-module, from a category $\mathcal W_\theta$ they introduce, and $V$ a $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module. For quantum affine algebras the action on $M\otimes V(z)$, $V$ finite dimensional, is a formal Laurent series [@appel_vlaar2024, Thm. 6.4.2]. When $M$ is the restriction of an irreducible finite-dimensional $U_q(\hat g)$-module and $V$ is irreducible, it is a scalar multiple of the **trigonometric tensor K-matrix** $R^{\rm norm}_{V^\psi M}(z)_{21}\,(1\otimes K^{\rm trig}_V(z))\,R^{\rm norm}_{MV}(z)$, which satisfies the generalized spectral reflection equation [@appel_vlaar2024, Thm. 6.5.2]. For the $q$-Onsager algebra every finite-dimensional irreducible module is such a restriction, by a theorem of Ito and Terwilliger quoted in [@appel_vlaar2024, Rem. 6.5.3(a)]; in general the conclusion holds whenever the relevant space of intertwiners is one-dimensional [@appel_vlaar2024, Rem. 6.5.3(b)].

In physical terms, $\mathbb K$ is the reflection matrix of a particle $V$ on a boundary carrying the boundary module $M$, and its factorization is (-@eq-dbd-fused-k) with $M$ a particle used as a defect: $\mathcal R$ lets the particle cross $M$, $\mathcal K$ reflects it at the bare boundary, and $\mathcal R^\psi_{21}$ brings it back. Appel and Vlaar's coideals are right coideals and their boundary module stands on the left; ours stand on the right, and $\omega_q$ translates as in @sec-letzter-kolb. Sklyanin used the same dressing to build reflection matrices on larger spaces [@sklyanin1988]. We checked the simplest case: for the sine-Gordon coideal with generic $\hat\epsilon$ and $\mathcal W=V(\theta_d)$, $\bar{\mathbb T}(1\otimes K)\mathbb T$ with $\mathbb T=\check R$ intertwines the coideal on $V(\theta)\otimes\mathcal W$, the space of such intertwiners is one-dimensional, and the reflection equation holds ($10^{-15}$, `textbook_code/defect_doubling.py`). By Remark 6.5.3(b) this matrix is therefore the trigonometric tensor K-matrix.

For a jump defect $\mathcal W$ is a module of a Borel subalgebra only, so (-@eq-dbd-fused-k) is outside Appel and Vlaar's categories, which need $U_q(\hat g)$-modules. Two remarks connect it with their work. First, by @prp-defect-fusion-k (3) the result is, sector by sector, an ordinary trigonometric K-matrix with shifted parameters. Second, Appel and Vlaar note that in quasi-split type $\mathbb K$ lies in a completion of $U_q(\mathfrak k)\otimes U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$, and propose evaluating the second leg on infinite-dimensional Borel modules to obtain Baxter-type relations for boundaries [@appel_vlaar2024, Sec. 1.6.2], the boundary counterpart of the Q-operators of @sec-q-operators. Defects in front of boundaries are a natural physical setting for that programme.

## Boundaries and non-invertible symmetries {#sec-noninvertible-boundaries}

**Lines fused onto boundaries.** A topological line placed next to a boundary can be moved onto it, and the result is again a boundary. In rational conformal field theory, fusing a Verlinde line onto a Cardy boundary decomposes by the fusion coefficients; the Lee–Yang defect $\Phi$ fused onto the boundary $\mathbb 1$ gives the boundary $\Phi$ (@sec-defect-lee-yang), and Runkel showed that perturbed $(1,s)$ defects fused onto the Cardy boundary $(1,1)$ give the perturbed $(1,s)$ boundaries [@runkel2010] (@sec-perturbed-defects). In the massive theory the fused reflection matrix is (-@eq-dbd-fused-k). For an invertible line, $\mathcal W=\mathbb C$ and $\mathbb T=g$, it is $g^{-1}Kg$: the boundary transformed by the symmetry, which is invariant exactly when $K$ intertwines $g$.

**Lines ending on boundaries.** A line can also end on a boundary, at a topological junction in ${\rm Hom}(L\otimes B,B)$. Shimamori and Yamaguchi call a boundary $B$ weakly symmetric under a fusion category of lines if this space is non-zero for every line $L_a$ [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, after eq. (1.3)]. Every line can then be pushed onto the boundary, and the boundary amplitudes obey Ward–Takahashi identities. An example is the sum of all Cardy states, $\sum_c\lvert L_c\rangle$ [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, footnote 13].

**Modified boundary crossing.** Shimamori and Yamaguchi studied the kinks of the minimal models $\mathcal M_p$ perturbed by $\phi_{1,3}$, $p\ge4$, whose $p-1$ vacua are permuted by the non-invertible symmetry $A_p$ (@sec-topological-lines). A kink $K_{ab}(\theta)$, with $a$ the outer vacuum, reflects into $K_{ac}(-\theta)$ with amplitude $R^a_{bc}(\theta)$ [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eq. (3.1)]. The amplitudes obey boundary unitarity and the boundary Yang–Baxter equation in the usual form, and, when the symmetry is spontaneously broken and $B$ is weakly symmetric, the modified crossing relation
$$
R^b_{ca}\Big(\frac{i\pi}2-\theta\Big)=\sum_d\sqrt{\frac{d_d}{d_b}}\;S^{ba}_{cd}(2\theta)\,R^d_{ca}\Big(\frac{i\pi}2+\theta\Big)
$$ {#eq-dbd-sy-crossing}
[@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eqs. (3.29)–(3.32)], with $d_a=\sin\frac{a\pi}p/\sin\frac\pi p$ and $S$ the bulk kink S-matrix in the normalization of Copetti, Córdova and Komatsu. Without the factor $\sqrt{d_d/d_b}$ this is Ghoshal and Zamolodchikov's boundary crossing-unitarity. The factor comes from the normalization of the kink states: the boundary contributes a constant $C^B_{ab}=1/(d_bF^B_b)$ that does not depend on the outer vacuum and cancels, so only the bulk factor of Copetti, Córdova and Komatsu survives [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eqs. (3.22)–(3.28)].

**Consequences.** The Ward–Takahashi identities of the lines reduce to those of $L_2$ [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eqs. (4.2)–(4.3)]. For $p\ge5$ they forbid all non-diagonal reflections and make all diagonal ones equal, without using integrability [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eq. (4.12)]. For $p=4$, the tricritical Ising model, the boundary Yang–Baxter equation and crossing leave two scenarios, purely diagonal or purely off-diagonal reflection [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eqs. (4.26)–(4.27)]. In both cases the minimal solution of crossing and unitarity is a ratio of Gamma-function products of the Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov type [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eqs. (4.29), (4.35)].

**Relation to @sec-topological-lines.** In the bulk, the modified crossing rule of Copetti, Córdova and Komatsu is equivalent to ordinary crossing after a rapidity-dependent renormalization of the kink states, $(d_x/d_y)^{i\theta/2\pi}$ for a kink from $x$ to $y$ (@exr-modified-crossing); Shimamori and Yamaguchi record the corresponding bulk factor [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eq. (2.32)]. The same renormalization works at the boundary. With $\hat R^a_{bc}(\theta)=(d_bd_c/d_a^2)^{i\theta/2\pi}R^a_{bc}(\theta)$ and the conventionally normalized bulk S-matrix, (-@eq-dbd-sy-crossing) becomes Ghoshal and Zamolodchikov's crossing relation: the $\theta$-dependent factors cancel against those of the bulk S-matrix at $2\theta$, and the shifts by $\frac{i\pi}2$ produce exactly $\sqrt{d_d/d_b}$ (@exr-dbd-boundary-crossing, by hand). Unitarity and the boundary Yang–Baxter equation are unchanged by the renormalization. So, as in the bulk, crossing alone cannot tell the two normalizations apart; the Ward–Takahashi identities can, because the action of the lines on kink states is not invariant under rapidity-dependent rescalings.

**Relation to the defects of this part.** The integrable defects of Part VIII are topological lines that are not symmetries: they act on particles through rapidity-dependent transmission matrices, and the invertible lines appear only in their limits (@prp-defect-twist-limit). In the doubled theory a topological line becomes a boundary, and this chapter has identified the boundary symmetries: a twisted diagonal for an invertible line, two Borel halves for a jump defect. For the non-invertible lines of Copetti, Córdova and Komatsu and of Shimamori and Yamaguchi, which act on vacua rather than on the particles' internal labels, the corresponding doubled boundaries and their symmetry algebras have not been worked out.

## Exercises {#sec-defect-boundary-exercises}

::: {#exr-dbd-cop}
Show that $P\check R(x_1/x_2)P$ intertwines $\Delta^{\rm op}$, and that the doubled bulk S-matrix of @sec-doubling-trick commutes with (-@eq-dbd-coproduct). Show that $\Delta_A$ is coassociative. Why does the same S-matrix not commute with the coproduct of $U\otimes U$? Show that $\omega_q$ is a Hopf algebra isomorphism $U^{\rm cop}\to U$ and that $V(1/y)\circ\omega_q=\bar V(y)$ for the $a_n$ vector representation.
:::

::: {#exr-dbd-diagonal-coideal}
Prove (-@eq-dbd-diagonal), and deduce that $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$ is a left coideal subalgebra of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$ for every Hopf automorphism $\psi$. Show that $\omega_q\otimes{\rm id}:U\otimes U^{\rm cop}\to U\otimes U$ reverses the coproduct and maps $\Delta(U)$ onto Bao and Wang's right coideal $(\omega\otimes1)\Delta(U)$. Is $\Delta(U)$ a coideal of $U\otimes U$?
:::

::: {#exr-dbd-invertible}
For sine-Gordon solitons, find the automorphism $\psi$ implemented by the twist line $\mathbb T={\rm diag}(e^{i\alpha},e^{-i\alpha})$ and by the charge-conjugation line $\mathbb T=\sigma_x$, and show that their doubled boundaries are invariant under $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$. What happens to the spectral parameter if $t_0t_1\ne1$?
:::

::: {#exr-dbd-mixed-twist}
For the type-I$_-$ matrix with $A_n=q^{-n}$, $D_n=q^{n+s}$, $C_n=-i(y/y_d)q^{-n}$, $B_n=-i(y/y_d)q^{n+s}$, write out the equation $\mathbb T\big(\pi(e_1)\otimes1+\pi(k_1)\otimes Y\big)=\big(Y\otimes1+\kappa\otimes\pi(e_0)\big)\mathbb T$ on $v_\pm\otimes\lvert n\rangle$, with $Y\lvert n\rangle=Y_n\lvert n+1\rangle$ and $\kappa\lvert n\rangle=\kappa_n\lvert n+2\rangle$. Show that $Y_{n+1}-Y_n=-iy_dq^{-2n-2-s}$ and $\kappa_n=q^{-2n-2-s}$, independently of $y$. Derive (-@eq-dbd-second-module), verify its relations, and show that $\rho(k_1)\tilde\rho(k_1)=q^4\tilde\rho(k_1)\rho(k_1)$.
:::

::: {#exr-dbd-e-one}
Show that a subalgebra of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$ that contains $k_1\otimes k_1$ and $e_1\otimes1+k_1\otimes e_0$ contains $e_1\otimes1$ if $q^4\ne1$. Show that the doubled boundary of the type-I$_-$ defect is not invariant under $e_1\otimes1$ for any action $Z$ on $\mathcal W$. *Hint:* compare the terms of order $y^2$.
:::

::: {#exr-dbd-fusion-gz}
Compute the charge-sector blocks of (-@eq-dbd-fused-k) for the type-I$_-$ matrix and $K_D={\rm diag}(ye^{i\eta}+y^{-1}e^{-i\eta},ye^{-i\eta}+y^{-1}e^{i\eta})$, and compare with Corrigan and Zambon's (2.18). Show that the blocks are (-@eq-bsg-k-matrix) with $\hat\epsilon_{1,0}=-\cos(\eta_D\mp i\lambda\theta_d)/\sin\pi\lambda$ after a diagonal change of basis. Then use the classical limit of @cnj-bsg-uv-ir and $C_{0,1}=\cosh(\theta_d^{\rm cl}\pm\frac{i\beta_{\rm SG}\phi_D}2)$ to derive $\lambda\theta_d=(\lambda+1)\theta_d^{\rm cl}$.
:::

::: {#exr-dbd-classical-dressing}
Prove @prp-fused-bdg (1). Why does $L_d^{-1}$, not $L_d$, appear in (-@eq-dbd-dressed-k)? For $a_2^{(1)}$ with a Neumann boundary for $\vec\psi$, write the boundary conditions of the fused system and identify the boundary variables.
:::

::: {#exr-dbd-boundary-crossing}
Let $\tilde S^{ab}_{dc}(\theta)=(d_ad_c/d_bd_d)^{i\theta/2\pi}S^{ab}_{dc}(\theta)$ be the conventionally normalized kink S-matrix [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eq. (2.32)] and $\hat R^a_{bc}(\theta)=(d_bd_c/d_a^2)^{i\theta/2\pi}R^a_{bc}(\theta)$. Show that (-@eq-dbd-sy-crossing) is equivalent to $\hat R^b_{ca}(\frac{i\pi}2-\theta)=\sum_d\tilde S^{ba}_{cd}(2\theta)\hat R^d_{ca}(\frac{i\pi}2+\theta)$, and that boundary unitarity and the boundary Yang–Baxter equation take the same form for $R$ and $\hat R$.
:::

## Notes and references {#sec-defect-boundary-notes}

Bajnok and George introduced the doubling trick and the fusion of a defect onto a boundary [-@bajnok_george2006]; Bajnok and Simon used fusion to solve the sinh-Gordon and Lee–Yang defects and found the classical fusion onto Dirichlet and Neumann boundaries [-@bajnok_simon2008]; Corrigan and Zambon fused type-I and type-II defects onto sine-Gordon boundaries with reflection matrices that keep track of the boundary charge, and related the result to Habibullin's construction of the general boundary condition from two Bäcklund transformations [-@cz2012]. Dynamical boundaries are due to Baseilhac, Delius and George [-@bdg2002], with the quantum version and the $q$-Onsager algebra due to Baseilhac and Koizumi [-@baseilhac_koizumi2003; -@baseilhac_koizumi2005]. Quantum symmetric pairs of diagonal type, with the quasi-R-matrix as their intertwiner, are discussed by Bao and Wang [-@bao_wang2018b, Rem. 4.10(2)] and in Wang's survey [-@wang2023]; the general quasi-K-matrix is due to Bao and Wang [-@bao_wang2018] and Balagović and Kolb [-@balagovic_kolb2019], and universal K-matrices of Kac–Moody type to Kolb [-@kolb2014] and Appel and Vlaar [-@appel_vlaar2022]. Tensor K-matrices are due to Appel and Vlaar [-@appel_vlaar2024], building on Sklyanin's dressing [-@sklyanin1988] and on Kolb's braided module categories. Modified crossing for non-invertible symmetries is due to Copetti, Córdova and Komatsu [-@cck2024; -@cck2025], and its boundary version to Shimamori and Yamaguchi [-@shimamori_yamaguchi2025]. The coideal $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$ description of the doubled theory, @prp-reflected-copy (3), @prp-diagonal-coideal (4), @prp-diagonal-borel, the outcome of @cnj-twisted-diagonal, the parameter map and scalar identity of @prp-defect-fusion-k (3)–(4), @prp-fused-bdg, and the renormalization of @exr-dbd-boundary-crossing are stated here.

Corrections and clarifications to the sources made in this chapter:

- **Diagonal type.** Bao and Wang's remark [@bao_wang2018b, Rem. 4.10(2)] is made in the finite-type setting of their paper, with "one checks" for the coideal property. Kolb [@kolb2014] and Appel and Vlaar [@appel_vlaar2022] assume an indecomposable Cartan matrix, so their universal K-matrices do not cover the diagonal type of affine algebras, whose Cartan matrix is that of $\hat g\oplus\hat g$. Their right coideal $(\omega\otimes1)\Delta(U)$ corresponds to the left coideal $\Delta(U)\subset U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$ of the doubled theory through $\omega_q\otimes{\rm id}$. The phrase "of diagonal type" in Kolb and Yakimov [@kolb_yakimov2020] refers to Nichols algebras with diagonal braiding and is unrelated.
- **Corrigan and Zambon (2.18)** [@cz2012]. The fused type-I reflection matrix, which they call equivalent to the full Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov solution, is in book conventions (-@eq-bsg-k-full) with $(\eta,\vartheta)=(\eta_D,\lambda\theta_d)$, and the equality extends to the scalar factors: no CDD factor appears. Their $\hat T(\theta)=T(-\theta)^{-1}$ is the book's $\bar{\mathbb T}$.
- **Shimamori and Yamaguchi** [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025]. Their modified boundary crossing (3.29) is equivalent to the conventional crossing of Ghoshal and Zamolodchikov for amplitudes renormalized by the same rapidity-dependent kink factors that relate the two normalizations of the bulk S-matrix (their (2.32)); what distinguishes the normalizations is the Ward–Takahashi identities, not crossing (@exr-dbd-boundary-crossing, by hand).
- **Book-internal: the pre-registered @cnj-twisted-diagonal** is refuted as stated, and the expected diagonal Borel symmetry is confirmed. In addition, the opposite Borel subalgebra survives twisted by charge conjugation, on a second module structure of $\mathcal W$ (@prp-diagonal-borel). This refines, without contradicting, the statement of @sec-perturbed-defects that no action of the $e_j$ on $\mathcal W$ extends the $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$ symmetry with the untwisted coproduct.
